'''Vadim Alekseyevich Kuzmin''' ({{langx|ru|Вади́м Алексе́евич Кузьми́н}}; 16 April 1937 – 17 September 2015) was a Russian theoretical physicist.

==Biography==
Kuzmin completed his undergraduate studies in 1961 at [[Moscow State University]] and his PhD in 1971 at [[Lebedev Institute]]. He has been a member of the [[Institute for Nuclear Research]] in Moscow since its founding in 1970. There, he became a professor and chair of the department of [[particle astrophysics]] and [[cosmology]]. In 1987, he obtained the Russian doctoral title.

In 1966, he and [[Georgiy Zatsepin]] predicted (what is now called) the [[Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin limit|GZK limit]] for [[cosmic rays]].<ref name="Zatsepin">{{cite journal| last=Zatsepin| first=G. T.| last2=Kuz'min| first2=V. A.| year=1966| title=Upper Limit of the Spectrum of Cosmic Rays| journal=Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Physics Letters| volume=4| pages=78&ndash;80| bibcode=1966JETPL...4...78Z | url=http://www.jetpletters.ac.ru/ps/1624/article_24846.pdf}}</ref>

In neutrino physics, he proposed an experiment using [[gallium]]/[[germanium]] detectors to detect low-energy [[solar neutrino]]s. In 1970, he proposed [[neutron-antineutron oscillations]] as a possibility for observing violation of [[baryon number]].

Also in 1970, he independently discovered the [[Baryogenesis#Sakharov conditions|Sakharov conditions]]. 

In the 1980s, he was a pioneer in the theory of [[electroweak interactions|electroweak]] [[baryogenesis]]. In 1985, his influential work with [[Valery Rubakov]] and [[Mikhail Shaposhnikov]] estimated the rate of anomalous electroweak process that violated [[baryon number]] conservation in the cosmic plasma of the early universe.<ref>{{cite journal| first1=V. A.| last1=Kuzmin| first2=V. A.| last2=Rubakov| first3=M. E.| last3=Shaposhnikov| title = On anomalous electroweak baryon-number non-conservation in the early universe| journal = Physics Letters B| volume = 155| date = 1985-05-16| issue = 1–2| pages = 36–42| doi= 10.1016/0370-2693(85)91028-7|bibcode = 1985PhLB..155...36K }}</ref>

In 1999 the Russian Academy of Sciences awarded Kuzmin and Rubakov the [[Friedmann Prize]] "for a series of works on the formation of the baryon asymmetry of the universe".<ref name="RAS">{{cite web | title=Премия имени А.А. Фридмана| trans-title=A. A. Friedmann Prize| website=Russian Academy of Sciences| url=http://www.ras.ru/win/db/award_dsc.asp?P=id-78.ln-ru| language=ru| access-date=25 September 2018| quote=За серию работ "Образование барионной ассиметрии Вселенной"}}</ref>

In 2000, he became a corresponding member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]. In 2003, he received the [[Institute for Nuclear Research]] [[Markov Prize]] for his contributions to neutrino physics.<ref name="INR RAS">{{cite web| title=INR Markov Prize| website=Institute for Nuclear Research| url=https://www.inr.ac.ru/a/i/6441e.htm| access-date=25 September 2018}}</ref> In 2006, he received the [[Pomeranchuk Prize]] "for his pioneering work on baryon-number violating processes, baryogenesis, and on the fundamental properties of high-energy cosmic rays", together with [[Howard Georgi]].<ref name="ITEP">{{cite web | title=Pomeranchuk Prize Winners 2006| website=ITEP| url=https://www.itep.ru/science/pomeranshuk/detail.php?ID=511| access-date=26 September 2018}}</ref>
